authoritative_for: Vizier owns its private implementation-run ledger, exact input and generated documents, work-packet graph, Nucleus correlations, workspace leases, Git candidate identities, review dispositions, bounded remediation, configured gate evidence, recovery, and domain success.
The selected ledger and exact recorded Git objects are authoritative for Vizier workflow state and candidate identity.
not_authoritative_for: The caller owns requirements, contract-unit boundaries, terminology freshness, repository and gate authority, and permission to apply, push, release, or deploy a result; Git owns repository object semantics.
Nucleus owns bounded agent execution, authentication, job and attempt state, cancellation, and managed-tool transport, but not Vizier workflow or success.

covers: All supported public Vizier outcomes for implementation delegation, workflow and installation operation, and development in this release.
excludes: Help and version display, internal managed-tool handlers, direct SQLite access, Pratica or Semantics operation, applying a candidate to the caller's branch, push, release, deployment of another product, and current runtime readiness are outside this inventory claim.

shared_access_and_trust: Vizier is a short-lived current-user CLI; callers select one private ledger and one authorized Git repository, while Nucleus jobs receive only their role-specific workspace and explicitly frozen run material.
Catalog presence grants no authority to mutate a repository, retry work, cancel a run, deploy Vizier, or publish a release.
shared_privacy_and_retention: Vizier and correlated Nucleus state may retain complete private briefs, contracts, terminology, plans, repository context, diffs, prompts, tool calls, handoffs, and reviews without an automatic pruning horizon.
Release and Chancery bundles contain program and public documentation only, never private run or repository material.
compatibility_and_retirement: Provider release, entry contract versions, ledger schema, document and toolset identities, Nucleus protocol, and Git object formats are separate compatibility axes.
Incompatible workflow, state, requester, or installation meaning requires successor contracts and recovery proof before older behavior is retired.
operational_limits: Vizier coordinates finite implementation runs with one broad review of the assembled delegation, packet graph, and current packet plans, one broad review per packet candidate, one broad integrated review, and persisted-scope bounded targeted rechecks; it is not a daemon, general scheduler, workflow engine, requirements parser, deployment orchestrator, or release gate.
No run duration, queue time, model quality, repository size, retained-history, throughput, release, deployment, or availability objective is promised.
